title: Training Frontline Health Workers in Low- and Middle-Income Countries to Reduce Contraceptive Stock-Outs: Evidence from Indonesia
eligible_reason: The underlying design is a staggered binary adoption (health facilities receive inventory-management training at facility-specific months, never-trained facilities present), but every reported specification is weighted by coarsened-exact-matching (CEM) weights, i.e. matching-based DiD, and the TWFE specifications (Table 2, Figure 3) additionally include time-varying district/province controls and an extra regressor 'inter'; Figures 4-5 are IV. The analysis data (LMIS, Magpi, baseline-endline surveys) are protected under an MOU and the package contains only a synthetic LMIS file (one facility), so no specification is replicable from the package.
design_notes: Unit of observation: contraceptive product x health facility x month (facilproduct2 = product x facility id; facid = facility; edate2 = month, Jan 2015-Dec 2019). Treatment: training = 1 once the facility has received onsite (visitnum) or offsite (refresh) training; first_treat = month of first training (missing for never-trained); facilities receiving both types or multiple onsite visits are dropped. Table 2 (Table 2.do lines 6-9): reghdfe stockout2 inter <11 district/province controls> i.training [pw = cem_weights], absorb(product facid i.trend [+ district/province x trend or x month]) vce(cluster facid month). Figure 3b: same with L*event/F*event relative-time dummies (binned at 25 months). Figure 6 (event studies without controls but with CEM weights): 6a did_imputation stockout2 facilproduct2 edate2 first_treat2 [aw = cem_weights], allhorizons pretrend(25) fe(product2) cluster(facid); 6b csdid2 stockout2 [iw = cem_weights], ivar(facilproduct2) tvar(edate2) gvar(first_treat) method(drimp) cluster(facid); 6c eventstudyinteract stockout2 L*event F*event [pw = cem_weights], absorb(product2 facid trend) vce(cluster facid) cohort(first_treat) control_cohort(never_treated). Figures 4-5 use ivreghdfe with binary instruments for visit and refresher counts. Table 1 is a balance table. The number of adoption cohorts cannot be computed (synthetic data has a single facility).
estimators_reported: TWFE static with CEM weights and controls (Table 2)
TWFE event study with CEM weights and controls (Figure 3b)

ineligible_main_text_specs.reason: CEM matching weights; time-varying district and province controls; additional regressor inter; district/province trends in Columns 2-4
BJS, CSA and SA estimates weighted by CEM weights (matching-based); otherwise no controls, unit = facilproduct2, time = edate2, cohort = first_treat, never-treated controls

data_files_note: data files/LMIS Data_Synthetic.dta (synthetic, 1 facility), Magpi Data_Synthetic.dta, Baseline-Endline Surveys_Synthetic.dta; INDO-DAPOER_District.dta and _Province.dta are real public control data. README: MOU with JSI prohibits sharing; synthetic data are 'not to replicate the results'.
software_detail: Stata/MP 16.1 (reghdfe, ivreghdfe, csdid/csdid2, did_imputation, eventstudyinteract, event_plot, cem); R for IV preparation
screener_notes: Borderline on the matching rule: if the team treats CEM weights as allowed analysis weights, Figure 6a-6c would be eligible modern-estimator specifications (binary training, facility-specific first_treat, never-treated controls, product + facility + month FE, cluster facid) with a constructible TWFE counterpart. Replication would still require the MOU-protected LMIS data from JSI. Also note did_imputation's fe(product2) option may replace the default unit and period FE, which should be checked against the text if the paper is ever pursued.
